So, I originally posted this idea in /v/gaming regarding the reduction of minimalistic-content posts (i.e. shitposts), but I think this is something that could benefit the site and move to differentiate its community in a positive manner.

/r/gaming was hardly unique in having a problem with shitposts. (Memes, pictures, DAE, etc) At least half the subreddits I'd subscribed to had shitposts for half their content. Is there something that could be done site-wide to better allow people to control the content they see?

What if every subverse had multiple categories. (For lack of a better name) /v/ is the generic, all-inclusive. If you go to /v/gaming (the example I'll be using) you see every post submitted.

But then there's a button that takes you to /c/gaming where it's just the casual content - things related to the topic, but not exactly discussing it. Pictures and memes and DAE and stuff. Ya know, shitposts. It's content, and sometimes worth a laugh. To each their own.

And then there's /s/gaming where serious content goes. Links to news articles and actual discussions of topics and trends in gaming. And maybe there's other categories worth thinking.

When you submit a link, you're asked which category it belongs to. By default, the /c/ is selected. Checkbox /s/ and it's marked as a serious post. (Why /c/ by default? Minimal-effort posts more likely to be made with minimal effort.) In a user's preferences/settings, they're asked what default category they want to see when they enter a subverse. People who want memes and pictures can have their way, and those who don't can have theirs.

Basically, it allows the community to keep the mass of content shitposts provide wile allowing users who don't want to see that (or only want to see that) the option of choosing. It takes a good chunk of burden off mods to delete posts and reiterate rules endlessly. It's a lot of work up-front for a large benefit in the long-run.

TL;DR: Can Voat offer user-activated content filtering as a site-wide level?
